quandoUsar: Comparing structured records in columns, letting the user sort by any of them: projects, invoices, team members.
Selecting several rows for a bulk action: `selectable` adds the checkbox column, selection by clicking the row, range selection with `Shift`, and the count in the footer.
Tables that fit entirely on the page, where sorting can happen in the browser.
quandoEvitar: Use `tree-table` when rows have children and sorting must respect the hierarchy.
Use `comparison-table` to compare plans or products feature by feature, with one highlighted column.
Large collections or ones sorted on the server call for another solution: sorting is local, all rows go into the DOM, and there is no prop to control the order from outside.

teclado.acao: On a header, sort by the column; again, toggle between ascending and descending.
On a checkbox, check or uncheck the row; on the header checkbox, all rows.
In the header, move focus between the select-all checkbox and the sort buttons.
Move focus between the row checkboxes; from the first row, `↑` goes up to the select-all checkbox, and from it `↓` goes back down.
Go to the first or last header control, or to the first or last row checkbox.
Clears the selection when rows are checked.

acessibilidade: It is a native `<table>` with a hidden `caption` and explicit ARIA roles, which keep the semantics when CSS redraws it on narrow screens; sortable headers carry `aria-sort`.
A `role="status"` region announces the column and direction of the sort and how many rows are selected; the header checkbox uses the indeterminate state.
Each row's checkbox is named by the value of the first column; the fixed texts (`Sort by`, `Select all rows`, `Clear selection`) are in English.
movimento: When sorting, rows glide on a spring to the new position over a fixed band that tints the sorted column; the arrow appears on the column and rotates when the direction flips.
The checkbox mark draws itself and, in the header, morphs between check and dash; the footer count swaps text rising or descending, with the width following.
With “reduced motion” on, rows swap places instantly and texts merely alternate, with no displacement or blur.
responsivo: In windows up to 620 px the header becomes a scrollable strip of sort buttons and each row folds into two: first column and first number on top, the rest below.
The rule is a window media query, not a container query: in a narrow panel on a wide screen the table keeps a 560 px minimum width and scrolls horizontally.
desempenho: There is no pagination or virtualization, and each row is a `motion.tr` with a layout animation: for long collections, slice `rows` and combine with `pagination`.
Column widths are measured once and locked with `table-layout: fixed`, so sorting doesn't cause reflow; the measurement only repeats if the columns change.
notasIA: Pass `rows`, `columns` (`{ key, label, render?, numeric?, width? }`), and `rowKey`; every column is sortable unless it has `sortable: false`.
Sorting uses the raw value of `row[key]`, not what `render` returns: keep numbers and `Date` in the data and format only in `render`; empty values always go last.
Sorting is internal only (`defaultSort` and `onSortChange`); selection can be controlled with `selectedKeys` and `onSelectionChange`, and the first column should identify the row.
